We takedref = 4.6µm for the design-rule coupler [Figs. 5(b) and 5(c)] because its minimum edge gap, 1.05µm, matches that of the CD coupler of the fixed-spacing reference (1.06µm), so that the two are compared at the same lithography. It maintainsP+> 0.99over 274 nm
at a minimum edge gap of 1.05µm

In beam propagation method (BPM) simulations on a polymer platform, a 500µm coupler designed this way, without numerical optimization, maintains>99%transfer over 274 nm at a minimum edge gap of 1.05µm, compared with 150 nm for the CD coupler of a fixed-spacing reference at nearly the same gap.
CLM-PHOT-0132.statement: The 500 µm design-rule counter-diabatic coupler maintains greater than 99% supermode transfer over a 274 nm wavelength range.

extra_quotes: We perform the BPM simulations of Secs. 4–7 using a scalar 2D Crank–Nicolson BPM solver based on the finite-difference approach (∆x = 0.03µm,∆ z = 0.5µm) with a 4µm absorbing layer at the edges of a 48µm window [37].
The present analysis has limits. The design study uses 2D scalar BPM on a low-contrast polymer platform without material dispersion.
